title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated video and synthetic social media profiles were used to make a real, named attorney appear to offer services he does not provide. The failure is not a malfunction of a deployed commercial AI product but a deliberate misuse of AI generation tools by outside actors to manufacture convincing false identities at scale. The harm reached victims before any platform or authority intervention, because the fake profiles multiplied across multiple social networks and directed victims to off-platform payment channels where no institutional safeguard existed.

The scale reported, nearly 6,500 fake profiles removed across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, shows that platform detection did not catch the content proactively. Removal required a separately hired anti-piracy firm acting on behalf of the attorney's practice, meaning the burden of identification and takedown fell on the impersonated individual rather than the platforms. The scheme worked by exploiting trust in a recognizable professional identity, then routing victims through private messaging and peer-to-peer payment apps that leave little recourse after funds transfer.

What is not established is who the scammers are, whether any criminal investigation has produced findings, and whether the victims who lost money have any avenue for recovery.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Immigration attorney Angel Leal, who has practiced law in South Florida for over 30 years, reports that scammers are using artificial intelligence to impersonate him and defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos showing Leal offering immigration services he never provides, including US residency assistance for $2,200. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, though suspicious activity first appeared in October.

An anti-piracy company hired by Leal's firm has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct people to contact a number via WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal is warning immigrants to verify identities before paying for legal services and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate.
